textBlocks.text: Instructions
Use black ink or ball-point pen.
Fill in the boxes at the top of this page with your name, centre number and candidate number.
Answer all questions.
Answer the questions in the spaces provided
there may be more space than you need.
Show all the steps in any calculations and state the units.
Some questions must be answered with a cross in a box. If you change your mind about an answer, put a line through the box and then mark your new answer with a cross.
Information
The total mark for this paper is 120.
The marks for each question are shown in brackets
use this as a guide as to how much time to spend on each question.
Advice
Read each question carefully before you start to answer it.
Keep an eye on the time.
Write your answers neatly and in good English.
Try to answer every question.
Check your answers if you have time at the end.
Answer ALL questions.
1 Rock salt is a mixture of salt and sand. Crystals of pure salt can be obtained from rock salt by using the method below.
Use words from the box to complete the sentences.
You may use each word once, more than once or not at all.
crystals dissolve evaporate filter solution solvent
Grind the rock salt into a fine powder.
Add the powder to hot water and stir to ... the salt.
Filter the mixture. The salt passes through the filter paper leaving behind the sand.
Boil the filtrate to ... some of the water.
Leave the saturated solution to cool so that ... of salt form.
Finally, the cold mixture to separate the crystals from the remaining solution.
(Total for Question 1 = 5 marks)
2 The three states of matter are solid, liquid and gas.
The diagram shows how the particles are arranged in each of these states.
(a) Use words from the box to show the changes of state labelled X, Y and Z. You may use each word once, more than once or not at all.
boiling condensing crystallisation diffusion freezing
(b) Which statement best describes the movement of the particles in a gas?
A The particles vibrate about fixed positions.
B The particles slide past one another.
The particles move freely.
D The particles do not move at all.
(c) The diagram shows apparatus that can be used to measure the melting point of a solid. The solid is placed in a small tube. The small tube is then put into a liquid contained in a beaker.
The liquid is gently heated and the temperature at which solid Q melts is recorded.
(i) Give the name of the apparatus labelled P.
(ii) Solid Q melts at $ 1 4 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}. $
Explain why water is not a suitable liquid to use in this experiment.
(iii) Suggest why the liquid in the beaker needs to be stirred constantly.
(Total for Question 2 = 7 marks)
3 Air is a mixture of gases.
The table gives the formulae of three gases and their approximate percentage by volume in a sample of dry, unpolluted air.
(a) (i) Give the names of the two main gases in the sample of air.
(ii) Give the name of the gas that makes up most of the remaining 0.96% of the air.
(b) State a use for $ \mathrm{N}_{2} $
(c) Give the name of a gas present in polluted air that causes acid rain.
(d) A student used this apparatus to find the percentage by volume of oxygen in a sample of air.
She used this method.
place some wet iron wool in the bottom of a test tube
invert the test tube in a beaker containing water
measure the height of the column of air in the test tube
leave the test tube for one week
measure the new height of the column of air
The table shows her results.
(i) Some of the iron turned into rust.
Write a word equation for this reaction.
(ii) Use the student's results to calculate the percentage of oxygen in this sample of air.
(e) The student left the apparatus for another week and measured the height of the column of air again.
From this measurement, how could she tell whether all of the oxygen in the test tube had been used up in the first week?
(Total for Question 3 = 9 marks)
4 This is a description of how the orange colouring can be extracted from rose petals.
crush the petals using a pestle and mortar
add the crushed petals to some ethanol in a beaker
heat to about $ 6 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ and stir to produce an orange solution
separate the orange solution from the petals
(a) (i) Suggest why ethanol is used instead of water.
(ii) Ethanol is a flammable liquid. Suggest how it could be heated safely.
(iii) How could the orange solution be separated from the petals?
(b) The orange colouring is analysed using chromatography and is found to consist of two different colours, red and yellow.
The diagram shows the chromatography paper at the start of the experiment.
Complete the diagram to show a possible result at the end of the experiment.
5 This apparatus can be used to make and collect carbon dioxide.
This is done by adding dilute hydrochloric acid to calcium carbonate.
(a) Give the names of the pieces of apparatus labelled A, B and C.
(b) When an excess of carbon dioxide is bubbled through limewater, reaction 1 occurs followed by reaction 2.
The equations for these reactions are
reaction 1
reaction 2 $ \mathrm{C a C O_{3}}(s)+\mathrm{H_{2} O}(l)+\mathrm{C O_{2}}(g)\rightarrow \mathrm{C a} \left(\mathrm{H C O}_{3}\right)_{2} (\mathrm{a q}) $
Suggest two observations that would be made when excess carbon dioxide is bubbled through limewater.
(c) Carbon dioxide is used in some fire extinguishers because it does not support combustion. State another property of carbon dioxide that makes it suitable for use in fire extinguishers.
(d) Carbon dioxide is slightly soluble in water. The solution formed has a pH of 5.6 Which is the best description of a solution of carbon dioxide in water?
A strongly acidic
B strongly alkaline
C weakly acidic
D weakly alkaline
(Total for Question 5 = 7 marks)
6 The table gives some data about the first six members of a homologous series of compounds called the alkanes.
(a) Complete the table by
giving the molecular formula of hexane
giving the relative formula mass of butane
suggesting the boiling point of pentane
(b) What does the data show about the relationship between boiling point and relative formula mass?
(c) The molecular formula of ethene is $ \mathrm{C_{2} H_{4}} $
Ethene and ethane are in different homologous series.
Explain how the formulae of these compounds show that they are in different series.
(d) (i) In the table, draw displayed formulae for the two alkanes with the molecular formula $ C_{4} H_{1 0} $
(ii) What is the name given to compounds that have the same molecular formula but different displayed formulae?
(e) The reaction between ethane and bromine $ \left(\mathrm{B r}_{2}\right) $ is similar to the reaction between methane and bromine.
(i) Write a chemical equation for the reaction between ethane and bromine.
(ii) What is the name given to the type of reaction that occurs when ethane reacts with bromine?
(iii) Suggest the condition necessary for this reaction to occur.
(Total for Question 6 = 12 marks)
7 Distress flares are used to attract attention in an emergency. The flares contain magnesium, which burns with a bright, white flame to form magnesium oxide.
(a) The reaction between magnesium and oxygen is exothermic. What is meant by the term exothermic?
(b) The diagram shows the electronic configuration of a magnesium atom.
Put a cross in a box to indicate the diagram that shows the electronic configuration of an oxygen atom.
A
B
C
D
(c) Magnesium ions and oxide ions are formed when magnesium reacts with oxygen. The diagram shows the electronic configuration and charge of a magnesium ion.
Put a cross in a box to indicate the diagram that shows the electronic configuration and charge of an oxide ion.
A
B
C
D
(d) A major use of magnesium oxide is as a refractory material, which is a material that can withstand very high temperatures.
Explain, in terms of its structure and bonding, why magnesium oxide has a very high melting point.
(e) Magnesium oxide is also used as an antacid. It helps relieve indigestion by neutralising hydrochloric acid in the stomach.
Give the name and formula of the salt produced when magnesium oxide reacts with hydrochloric acid.
Name.
Formula.
(Total for Question 7 = 9 marks)
BLANK PAGE
8 The table gives information about the first three elements in Group 1 of the Periodic Table.
(a) Which information shows that the elements have similar chemical properties? Give a reason for your choice.
Information
Reason.
(b) The elements in Group 1 show a clear trend (regular pattern) in some of their physical properties.
Identify the physical property that shows a clear trend.

(c) The elements also show a clear trend in their chemical properties, such as their reaction with water. When a small piece of lithium is added to water it fizzes gently and eventually disappears to form a solution.
(i) Describe a test to show that the gas given off is hydrogen.
(ii) Complete the equation for the reaction by inserting the state symbols.
(iii) State and explain the effect that the solution formed has on red litmus paper.
(d) State two similarities and two differences between the reactions of lithium and potassium with water.
Similarities
Differences
(e) When lithium burns in oxygen it forms lithium oxide $ \mathrm{(L i_{2} O)}。 $
(i) Write a chemical equation for the reaction between lithium and oxygen.
(ii) When sodium burns in oxygen, one of the products is sodium peroxide $ \mathrm{(N a_{2} O_{2})} $ Balance the equation to show the formation of sodium peroxide.
(Total for Question 8 = 14 marks)
9 A student investigates how temperature affects the rate of reaction between two colourless solutions containing ions.

When he mixes the solutions, a reaction takes place between the ions and after a while the mixture suddenly turns blue. He performs the experiment at five different temperatures and on each occasion he measures the time taken for the mixture to turn blue.
The table shows his results.
(a) (i) Plot the results on the grid and draw a curve of best fit.
(ii) Use your graph to estimate the time taken for the mixture to turn blue at $ 5 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $
(iii) What does the graph show about the relationship between temperature and time taken?
(b) Explain, in terms of particles, why an increase in temperature increases the rate of this reaction.
(c) State a variable that must be kept constant for the experiment to be valid (a fair test).
(Total for Question 9 = 9 marks)
10 A student investigates the reaction between dilute hydrochloric acid and marble chips. She uses this method.
put 50 $ cm^{3} $ of dilute hydrochloric acid into a polystyrene cup
measure the initial temperature of the acid
add 5.0 g of marble chips to the acid and stir the mixture
measure the temperature of the mixture after 2 minutes
She carries out the experiment three times, using different sizes of marble chips each time.
The diagram shows the temperatures for each experiment.
Experiment 1 large marble chips
Experiment 2 medium marble chips
Experiment 3 small marble chips
(a) Record the temperature readings in the table and calculate the temperature changes.
(b) Explain why the temperature change in experiment 2 is greater than the temperature change in experiment 1.
(c) Experiment 3 is repeated using $ 1 0 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of dilute hydrochloric acid in place of $ 5 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3}. $ The acid is in excess in both reactions.
State and explain how the temperature change would be different for $ 1 0 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of dilute hydrochloric acid.
(Total for Question 10 = 7 marks)
11 Titanium is extracted from its main ore, rutile, in a three-stage process.
Stage1 Rutile is heated with chlorine and coke (carbon) at a temperature of about $ 9 0 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $
Stage 2 $ \mathrm{T i C l}_{4} $ is then added to liquid magnesium at a temperature of about $ 8 0 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ in an atmosphere of argon.
During the reaction the temperature rises to about $ 1 1 0 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $
Stage 3 The magnesium chloride is removed by distillation from the mixture formed in stage 2, leaving behind pure titanium.
(a) In stage 1, is the carbon oxidised or reduced?
Give a reason for your answer.
(b) What does the reaction in stage 2 indicate about the reactivity of magnesium compared to the reactivity of titanium?
Explain your answer.
(c) In stage 3, suggest why distillation can be used to remove magnesium chloride from titanium.
(d) Titanium has these properties.
it is corrosion resistant
it has a high melting point
it has a very high strength-to-weight ratio
it is non-toxic
Complete the table to suggest an important property of titanium for each use.
Choose from the four properties listed.
You must choose a different property for each use.
(Total for Question 11 = 7 marks)
12 Magnesium reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid. The equation for the reaction is
(a) 0.0960 g of magnesium was added to $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of $ 0. 4 0 0 \mathrm{m o l} / \mathrm{d m}^{3} $ hydrochloric acid.
(i) Calculate the amount, in moles, of magnesium used.
(ii) Calculate the amount, in moles, of HCl in the $ 2 5. 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of hydrochloric acid.
(b) Use your answers from (a) to determine which of the reactants is in excess. Show your reasoning.
The reactant in excess is
(Total for Question 12 = 6 marks)
BLANK PAGE
13 The diagram shows the manufacture of ammonia by the Haber process and its conversion into the fertiliser ammonium nitrate.
(a) Give the names of the raw materials A and B.
(b) State the temperature, pressure and catalyst used to convert the mixture of nitrogen and hydrogen into ammonia.
temperature
pressure
catalyst...
(c) Give the name of the substance that has the formula $ \mathrm{H N O}_{3} $
(d) The equation for the formation of ammonium nitrate from ammonia is
25. 0 $ cm^{3} $ of a solution of ammonia of concentration 0.300 mol/dm $ ^{3} $ were reacted with a solution of $ HNO_{3} $
15. 0 $ cm^{3} $ of $ HNO_{3} $ were required to exactly neutralise the ammonia solution.
Calculate the concentration, in mol/dm $ ^{3} $ , of the $ \mathrm{H N O}_{3} $ solution.
(Total for Question 13 = 9 marks)
14 Carbon monoxide and hydrogen are used in the manufacture of methanol （ $ \mathrm{C H_{3} O H} $ ）.
The reaction is reversible and can reach a position of dynamic equilibrium.
The reaction is carried out at a pressure of about 100 atmospheres and a temperature of $ 2 5 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $
(a) State two features of a reaction that is in dynamic equilibrium.
(b) (i) How would a decrease in temperature at constant pressure affect the amount of methanol in the equilibrium mixture?
Explain your answer.
(ii) How would an increase in pressure at constant temperature affect the amount of methanol in the equilibrium mixture?
Explain your answer.

(c) Methanol $ \mathrm{(C H_{3} O H)} $ can be converted into methanal $ \mathrm{(H_{2} C O)} $ A mixture of methanol and oxygen is passed over an iron oxide catalyst at $ 2 5 0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ Methanal and water are the only two products. (i) Write a chemical equation for the conversion of methanol into methanal.
(ii) What is meant by the term catalyst?
(iii) Explain how a catalyst works.
(d) Methanol can be used in racing cars as an alternative fuel to petrol.
Write the chemical equation for the complete combustion of methanol.
(Total for Question 14 = 14 marks)
(TOTAL FOR PAPER = 120 MARKS)
BLANK PAGE
